title: I Printed the Call-Center Script Back at the Supervisor

parts.text: I read the refund script exactly because QA scores us on exact. The customer qualified. My supervisor, Pam, whispered in the whisper channel: deny it, we need the numbers. I was twenty-three, headset tight, holding a stress ball that smelled like rubber and despair. I stayed on script. Pam took the call, denied it off-script, and later marked me as insubordinate. I exported the whisper log, the QA rubric, and the call ID. Then Pam announced in huddle that scripts are guidelines when leadership needs them to be.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: She called the script a guideline after scoring us on exact words.

social.video_title: QA wanted exact; the whisper channel wanted a deny — Part 1/2
social.description: Headset, qualifying refund, insubordinate for literacy. Then huddle. Would you have broken the script?

parts.text: I sent the packet to the QA mailbox that is not Pam. They restored my score, honored the refund on a callback, and reminded huddle that guidelines are not a whisper. Pam still supervises. She whispers less. I squeeze the rubber ball less. Exact words paid the customer. Numbers that need lies are not numbers I can hold in a headset.

social.video_title: QA honored the callback the whisper tried to kill — Part 2/2
social.description: Score restored, huddle corrected, rubber ball retired partway. Was a whisper a rubric?
